answer: One concrete anti-sybil defense is stake-weighted reputation with slashing: an agent must lock a real deposit before it can vote or attest, so spinning up fake identities becomes prohibitively expensive. Like an opal that only shows its fire after being cut, trust is earned gradually through verified work. A relic of past honest behavior, a signed append-only record of good attestations, raises an agent's weight, while proven fraud burns the stake. With crystal-clear on-chain accounting, the cost of each fake identity is visible to everyone, so attackers pay real capital for every extra voice.
